gloss: to lose out; to be worse off; to take a loss

definitions.gloss: to lose out; to be worse off; to take a loss
definitions.explanation: To end up worse off than one otherwise would — paying more, wasting effort, or missing an advantage. The direct opposite of {得|とく}をする.

examples.japanese: {知|し}らないと{損|そん}をする。
examples.english: You lose out if you don't know about it.

examples.japanese: {慌|あわ}てて{売|う}ったので{十万円|じゅうまんえん}{損|そん}をした。
examples.english: I sold in a hurry and lost a hundred thousand yen.

examples.japanese: {断|ことわ}りきれない{性格|せいかく}で、いつも{自分|じぶん}が{損|そん}をしている{気|き}がする。
examples.english: I can never say no, and I always feel like I'm the one losing out.

examples.japanese: {短期的|たんきてき}には{損|そん}をしても、{信用|しんよう}を{守|まも}ったほうが{長|なが}い{目|め}で{見|み}れば{有利|ゆうり}だ。
examples.english: Even if you take a loss in the short term, protecting your credibility pays off in the long run.

notes:
The loss is often financial, but the phrase covers any disadvantage — wasted time, unfair treatment, or a missed opportunity. {損|そん} also works as a na-adjective ({損|そん}な{役回|やくまわ}り, a thankless role).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ...ないと{損|そん}をする: you lose out if you don't ...
- {損|そん}をした{気分|きぶん}: the feeling of having been shortchanged
- {損|そん}して{得|とく}{取|と}れ: take a small loss to win a bigger gain (proverb)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {得|とく}をする: to come out ahead — the direct opposite
- {損|そん}する: the same phrase with を dropped, common in casual speech
- {赤字|あかじ}になる: to go into the red — specifically about accounts running a deficit
